diagnoses.summary: High SPE with coherent T² movement; strongest evidence pointing to H2 PCV issue driving reactor pressure changes and vent flow abnormalities.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and high reactor pressure alarms. Evidence points to H2 PCV (vent) issues causing inadequate pressure relief in the CSTR, with the most likely being PCV stuck closed or degraded capacity.

The PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with strong reactor pressure increase driven mainly by the CSTR pressure and H2 vent behavior, with sensor alarms also triggered. The fixed-rule hypotheses indicate the H2 PCV likely failing, either stuck closed or capacity-degraded, consistent with high CSTR pressure and PCV-command vs actual mismatch.
High T2 and SPE with reactor pressure alarms point to a PCV-related pressure-control fault causing a coherent plant upset centered on the CSTR pressure/vent valve.
Abnormal PCA with coherent upset centered on the H2 PCV and reactor pressure; PCV related fault(s) most likely driving the upset.

A large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by reactor pressure/PCV related signals. Alarms indicate reactor pressure high (R_P_H, R_P_HH). The strongest fault candidates point to the hydrogen purge (PCV) path failing or degrading, leading to elevated CSTR pressure and vent flow changes.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset dominated by reactor pressure and H2 vent activity. Alarms indicate reactor pressure high. The strongest evidence points to an H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) fault, likely a PCV fault causing elevated CSTR pressure and abnormal vent behavior. The PCV appears to be the source of the SPE increase with pressure sensor readings and vent flow driving the mismatch.
Abnormal PCA with large, coherent upset dominated by CSTR pressure; likely H2 PCV issue causing reactor pressure rise and triggering high/high alarms.

The PCA flags a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure rise with concurrent high SPE, consistent with an H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) fault causing restricted venting and pressure buildup. The top evidence points to the H2 PCV path rather than sensor bias alone.

PCA abnormal with strong high T² and extremely high SPE, dominated by reactor pressure indicators and a known PCV issue. Likely H2 PCV fault causing reactor pressure rise and compensatory control actions.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure-side signals, with strong evidence pointing to H2 PCV (vent) related faults causing the high reactor pressure. The top contributor is CSTR pressure with a major share from CSTR H2 vent flow, and active alarms on reactor pressure high. This points to a PCV/vent issue rather than a purely sensor fault.

Coherent plant upset with reactor pressure rising and H2 vent flow likely constrained. High T2 and high SPE indicate a load/utility-type upset with a specific mechanism causing reactor pressure to push high, consistent with a stuck or degraded H2 PCV.

Abnormal state with high T² and high SPE, dominated by pressure- and vent-related signals; evidence points to the H2 PCV/vent subsystem being unable to relieve reactor pressure as required, with the pressure sensor and vent contributing to the anomaly.
A coherent plant upset dominated by reactor pressure rise with H2 vent involvement; likely H2 PCV fault causing pressure buildup and triggering high alarms.

The PCA monitor shows a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations, with a dominant contribution from the H2 vent (PCV) path and an alarm indicating reactor pressure high. The most consistent fault is a stuck PCV valve, causing reduced venting and pressure rise in the CSTR.

Abnormal PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE exceedances, dominated by reactor pressure event likely tied to the H2 vent (PCV). The strongest evidence points to PCV-related faults compromising venting and causing pressure rise.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations, driven mainly by reactor pressure dynamics and H2 vent (PCV) related signals. The strongest rule-based hypothesis points to an H2 PCV control fault causing high reactor pressure, with corroborating pressure readings and vent flow contributions.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with multiple alarms, dominated by a strong deviation at the top-tray temperature loop and reactor pressure rise. Evidence points to an H2 PCV actuator issue propagating through the main recirculation/reflux paths, with possible PCV capacity loss and a concurrent pressure-sensor bias contributing secondary effects.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations; strongest evidence points to a reflux-side disturbance causing column holdup reduction and temperature changes, consistent with a reflux-control fault. Multiple faults could be present, but reflux valve-related issue is most likely given top contributors and alarm.

A large, coherent plant upset with reactor pressure rising and H2 vent control issues, plus a high-pressure alarm pattern. Most likely a fault at the H2 PCV (vent) valve causing inadequate venting or mismatched command/actual (coherent upset).

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong H2 vent/signature and high reactor pressure alarms; likely a fault in the hydrogen vent (PCV) path causing abnormal venting/compliance, supported by top contributor being the CSTR H2 vent flow and related controller actions.

PCA abnormal with both T2 and SPE violations; strong evidence pointing to H2 PCV and related upstream pressure control issues causing a coherent upset propagating through the CSTR and column. Most likely a H2 PCV/stuck-closed condition with related downstream symptoms.

PCA signals a large, coherent process upset with large T2 and extreme SPE, dominated by H2 vent (PCV) related variables and column control signals, consistent with a H2 PCV fault propagating through the process (likely PCV actuation issue causing pressure rise and abnormal heat/temperature responses).

The PCA monitor shows a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by variables linked to reactor pressure/venting and column/condensation dynamics. The rule-based cues point strongly toward hydrogen vent issues at the CSTR and related condenser/reflux dynamics. The most consistent single fault is a problem with the H2 PCV (vent) acting abnormally, causing reactor pressure rise and downstream disturbances.
High-coherence plant upset with reactor pressure alarms and PCV-related faults; likely H2 PCV/condensing issues causing elevated pressure and distillate acetone deviation.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T2 and SPE, with dominant contribution from distillate acetone and column-related measurements, plus alarms suggesting high column pressure and distillate impurities. Rule-based hypotheses point to condenser cooling losses as the primary cause, with H2 PCV issues and control loop saturation contributing.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with two violations (high T2 and high SPE). The most contributing measurement is distillate acetone, with strong T2 and SPE influence, while multiple alarms point to high reactor pressure and a distressed condenser/reflux system. The likely root causes involve condenser cooling loss and H2 PCV issues, possibly with a secondary valve/pump constraint contributing to the upset.

A coherent but large process upset with high reactor pressure and a strong shift in distillate acetone signal, with condenser-related symptoms and PCV involvement; multiple faults possible but condenser cooling loss is the leading cause given the evidence.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous high T² and high SPE, driven by distillate acetone_pv and column conditions, with several alarms on reactor pressure. Most likely a condenser cooling/utility issue with secondary upsets from H2 PCV stance, leading to high reactor pressure and column disturbances.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with strong SPE violation and active alarms on column distillate and tray levels. Most likely root cause is condenser cooling effectiveness loss affecting the distillation train.

Normal operation PCA alarm with large coherent movement and also large SPE suggests a substantial process upset with possible sensor fault; multiple faults may be active, but the strongest evidence points to condenser cooling loss as the primary upset, with secondary sensor and valve issues contributing.

The PCA shows large coherent process movement with both T2 and SPE violated, dominated by a strong contribution from the distillate acetone measurement. The rule-based evidence points to condenser cooling issues as a primary driver, with secondary indications of H2 PCV issues and RB/LIC loop saturation.

Normal correlations are significantly broken with a large coherent upset suggesting a condenser-related issue propagating through the column. The strongest rule-based hypothesis points to condenser cooling effectiveness loss driving elevated distillate acetone signal and associated temperature/pressure responses.

Normal-operation PCA flag indicates a coherent plant upset with strong distillate acetone signal and high reactor pressure alarms. Most likely a condenser cooling issue propagating through the column, causing high acetone in distillate and column pressure concerns.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T2 and high SPE, most consistent with a condenser cooling issue propagating through the column, likely accompanied by H2 PCV related pressure effects. Multiple faults could be active, but the strongest evidence points to condenser cooling loss as the primary cause.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with significant SPE, dominated by distillate acetone measurement and TOP_TIC, pointing toward a condenser/condensation issue propagating through the column. Several rule-based hints align with condenser cooling effectiveness loss, with additional support for H2 PCV issues and a potential pressure-sensor bias. Likely multiple faults coexist, but the primary driver appears to be condenser cooling loss.

The PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong disturbance in the distillate acetone stream and related condenser/column behavior. The most likely root cause is condenser cooling effectiveness loss, with secondary contributions from H2 PCV issues and downstream feed/pressure anomalies.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with strong distillate acetone signal driving the response, and multiple alarms related to pressure and column operation. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling loss causing reduced condenser effectiveness and abnormal distillate composition, with secondary faults involving the H2 purge (PCV) path and RB loop regulation.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T² and high SPE, dominated by a distillate acetone anomaly and column/DP signals. The rule-based hints point to a condenser-related issue driving abnormal column behavior and an upstream PCV/supply pressure concern. Among catalogued faults, the most consistent single cause is condenser cooling loss, with secondary chances on upstream PCV and reflux flow faults that would explain the observed measurements and alarms.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong SPE indicating a process/system disturbance rather than a pure sensor anomaly. The most likely fault is a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness causing downstream column behavior to deviate and trigger column and distillate alarms.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with strong disturbance in distillate acetone signal and reactor pressure alarms; multiple fault hypotheses point to condenser/PCV issues propagating through the column. The most likely is condenser cooling loss causing poor condensation and elevated column pressure, with PCV-related faults also plausible given the pressure alarms.

PCA shows large, coherent upset with strong high T2 and SPE violations and distillate acetone signal dominates, with supporting alarms on column pressure and distillate flow. Faults consistent with a condenser-related upset propagate through the column.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous spikes in process variables and multiple alarms, dominated by distillate acetone deviation and reactor pressure/vent issues. The most plausible root cause is a condenser cooling/PCV-related fault propagating through the column and reactor. Multiple faults may be active.

PCA signals a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous severe T2 and SPE violations; most evidence points to a condenser cooling issue propagating through the column with high reactor pressure and a related PCV issue.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with strong distortion in distillate composition and reactor pressure drivers, pointing primarily to a H2 PCV issue propagating through the CSTR/tower system with condenser/tray interactions.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with strong indications centered around the distillation section, reactor H2 vent, and column TOP control. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling loss, with secondary hints pointing to H2 PCV issues and a reflux valve/stiction interaction affecting reflux flow and top tray conditions.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by abnormalities in the distillate acetone stream and elevated reactor/cstr pressures with H2 vent involvement. The most consistent fault names from the catalogue point to condenser-related upsets and H2 PCV issues causing pressure rise and disturbed column balance.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations. The leading indicators point to a condenser cooling issue driving a column disturbance, with a secondary suspicion on H2 PCV behavior affecting reactor pressure. Multiple faults could be active, but the most consistent with the evidence is condenser cooling loss, with possible PCV-related issues.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with high T2 and high SPE; strongest evidence points to a hydrogen purge/vent fault driving reactor pressure up, consistent with PCV actuator issues and related high-pressure alarms.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with concurrent T² and SPE violations. The strongest rule-based indication points to condenser issues affecting the distillation train, with secondary likelihood on H2 PCV faults given the reactor pressure alarms.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with strong SPE violations and multiple alarms (R_P_H, R_P_HH, DIST_X_L). The most consistent fault names point to pressure control issues around the CSTR/PCV and possible condenser inefficiency, with plausible PCV-related faults and a distillate leak contributing to the observed correlations.

The abnormal PCA state is most consistent with a fault in the H2 PCV actuator, specifically the PCV stuck closed, causing reactor pressure rise and compensatory responses across the column and vent system.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong deviation in both T2 and SPE, with high contribution from a H2 vent related signal and distillate acetone. Given active high-pressure alarms and the top contributors, the most plausible root causes are a H2 PCV fault driving the reactor pressure high and related process upsets (with condenser cooling issues as a secondary contributing factor).

PCA alarm with large coherent upset (high T²) and strong SPE indicating a root cause linked to H2 vent control and condenser performance. The top contributors point to H2 PCV related issues and associated pressure/flow disturbances, with distillate acetone deviation also contributing. Likely multiple faults centered on H2 PCV and condenser cooling effectiveness.

PCA flags a coherent plant upset with strong H2 vent-related disturbance and high reactor pressure alarms. The most plausible root cause is a fault in the H2 PCV/SOV area driving pressure rise and abnormal venting behavior, consistent with PCV actuator faults and related condenser/vent anomalies.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent disturbance and strong H2 system signal; primary fault is in the H2 PCV/vent system causing reactor pressure rise and related off-normal indicators. Condenser cooling loss and sensor bias are plausible secondary contributors.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with large, coherent movement driven by a likely H2 PCV fault causing reactor pressure rise; multiple sensors/controls reacting to this upset. The most likely fault is a stuck-closed H2 PCV (valve actuator issue) with possible concurrent PCV degradation.

A coherent reactor upset with high pressure in CSTR and active high-pressure alarms, strongly pointing to H2 vent control faults, especially PCV being stuck or degraded. The data also supports secondary issues in condenser cooling and possible sensor bias as alternatives.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with high T² and high SPE, dominated by a reactor pressure upset and signals pointing to the hydrogen vent (PCV) path and condenser/vapor handling. The most plausible root cause is an H2 PCV fault causing reactor pressure rise and abnormal venting behavior, with secondary contributions from condenser cooling/vent issues.

The PCA flag indicates a large, coherent plant upset with concurrent high T² and SPE, dominated by CSTR pressure/ventilation disturbances and steam/VOC handling. The fixed-rule hypotheses point to H2 PCV issues as the primary driver, with supporting effects on condenser/column behavior and sensor bias.
High-coherence plant upset with large T² and SPE, with strongest evidence pointing to condenser cooling issues in the distillation train.

Abnormal PCA with large, coherent upset affecting distillation heat removal and column conditions; strongest evidence points to condenser cooling being ineffective, with secondary hints of reflux flow issues.

PCA indicates a large coherent process upset with simultaneous normal-mode deviation (high T2 and high SPE). The strongest evidence points to a condenser cooling issue propagating through the column feeds and distillate stream.

PCA monitor flags a large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE violations. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling effectiveness loss affecting the distillation column, with secondary contributions from reflux flow issues and H2 PCV-related valve faults.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and a strong contribution from the condenser/column region, consistent with a condenser cooling issue propagating through the distillation train. Rule hints also point to condenser cooling loss as a primary cause, supported by the DIST_X_L alarm and distillate acetone deviation.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and an active DIST_X_L alarm. Rule-based hints point to condenser cooling effectiveness loss as the primary fault driving the abnormal state, with possible related issues in reflux flow control.

PCA alarm with large T² and SPE indicates a coherent process upset propagating through the plant, with distillate acetone concentration rising and distillate flow/temperature signals pulling the system. Most likely there is a condenser cooling effectiveness loss causing abnormal distillate composition and tray temperatures.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The strongest evidence points to a condenser-related upset propagating through the distillation section, consistent with a condenser cooling issue driving the abnormal correlations.

PCA flags a large coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, active DIST_X_L alarm on distillate acetone, and rule-based hints point to condenser/reflux issues driving the distillate acetone path. Most likely faults are condenser cooling loss or reflux valve stiction causing abnormal distillate acetone composition and column pressure/load propagation.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with high T2 and high SPE, with DIST_X_L alarm on distillate acetone and strong TOP_TIC influence. Most consistent fault is loss of condenser cooling effectiveness affecting the column performance and distillate composition.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with strong distortion at the distillation top and distillate composition signals, with an accompanying alarm on the distillate line. The most consistent fault is a condenser cooling loss causing degraded condenser effectiveness, supported by the DIST_X_L alarm and contribution from distillate composition and top temperature trends. Reflux valve issues and a possible top-temperature sensor freeze are plausible secondary faults given the same evidence, with a smaller likelihood of H2 PCV degradation.
